system.summary: Three layers used together inside one word, with clear French around the cipher runs. (1) Letters: drawn signs (27 shapes in the February letter, named G01-G27) and letter numbers below 30; most letters have two or three forms. (2) Syllables in rows of five by vowel (717 la, 718 le, 719 li; 891 ra, 892 re, 894 ro; 961 te, 962 ti). (3) Words and stems grouped by first letter between about 440 and 990 (444 avantage, 748 mesme, 775 Majeste, 950 sans), names lower (277 Suede). Not the image-55 key (K55) of the Høeg and Meyercron letters in targets/biermann1675, and not the Klingenberg cipher of targets/klingenberg1675.
system.notes: distinct_symbols is the 85 groups of the 22 February letter, on which the key was built: 27 signs, 12 letter numbers, 46 numbers of three digits (syllables and words). homophones.per_letter counts the forms seen in that letter. nomenclator.unread_groups counts 607 only in that letter; the three other letters hold 56 further groups with no value in key.tsv. No null has been shown; the unread sign G18 could be one.

prior_solution.where: None found; priority not established. Checked 15-16 Nov 2026: this repository (targets/biermann1675 lists the Lindenow letters as key unknown, not attempted); its issues and pull requests; web searches on Lindenow, Biermann, 1675 and cipher; Vaupell, Rigskansler Grev Griffenfeld (1880-82); Aarsberetninger fra det Kongelige Geheimearchiv VI. Not checked: the drafts of the copybook (TKUA Almindelig del 1 nr. 130) and Lindenow's own reports and legation papers of 1675 at the Rigsarkivet, which are on paper only.

solution.what: The four Lindenow letters and the clear Meyercron letter fetched from Arkivalieronline (images 14, 15, 22, 67-72, 130, 131); the repository's notes on the copybook saved with them.
22 February: 196 groups read from the scan by a helper session that had no key; the reading frozen before any decoding.
The 32 groups between the clear words 'a presenté est' and 'portant en substance' aligned word for word with the Meyercron sentence of 20 February: no consistent assignment.

The same 32 groups aligned with 'de la Suede' in place of 'du Roy son Maistre': 'tout entier a l'avantage de la Suede sans qu'il y ayt la moindre realite pour sa Majeste', with both 892 groups kept (moind-re re-alite). Letters, syllables and five word codes fixed.

The values carried through the other three cipher runs of the letter and the open groups read from context: 'l'armement de la Suede en Allemagne', 'les incommoditez', 'se peut faire c'est de plaindre leur malheur'. 24 values rest on one place each and on context alone; four more are single in the letter and recur only in the fitted April reading.
14 corrections to the frozen reading made against the scan and recorded (961 against 561, 20, 817, 894, the signs G26 and G27).

A candidate key frozen and applied once to the 12 April letter (image 130), transcribed without the key: 61 of 93 groups with a value; runs 'cette', 'il ne les', 'mesler en se', no continuous text. The candidate had 24 = n, later corrected to a from the February letter, so the pass does not test the present key.

12 April read further from context (a marriage proposal for a princess): some 25 values proposed, with three conflicts left open (ensemule for ensemble, 13 or 15, 10 where s is wanted). None taken into the key.
The key volume TKUA Chiffer 1670-1709, images 307-309, looked at again (309 mirrored and contrast-raised): no sheet for this family; 307 has 277 = Sielland.

Independent review by Claude Fable 5.2: all 196 groups read on the scan with no difference (not blind); the key applied by a second script; verdict revise, a partial reading only. Findings: 30 single values labelled 'supported'; the clause with 880 and 942 rests on two single values; stems in D listed for 607 against the number order.
607 with the signs r and G18 tried as expulser, exclure, esloigner, empescher: several fit the syntax, none is fixed. Left unread.
Drafts of the copybook, Lindenow's reports and legation papers located in the Rigsarkivet catalogue (paper only, not seen); Vaupell and Aarsberetninger VI searched: no text of this letter.
11 January, 18 January and 12 April checked on the scan by Claude Fable 5.2: three groups changed (858, 559, 15).

The key as it stands applied to the three other letters (decode.py): 33 of 57, 12 of 14 and 85 of 123 groups with a value; runs of French, no sentence. The letters had been seen during the work on the key, so this is a cross-letter check, not a held-out test.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 194 tokens, 83 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -1.76 per letter; random keys -3.191 (z 10.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.048 (mean -2.061, z 22.0); annealer on the real text -1.978. Verdict: pass.

The repository's statistical validation (docs/_validate.py, model fr-1600-letters) on the 22 February letter: reading -1.760 against random keys of the same structure -3.191 (z 10.1) and keys annealed onto the shuffled ciphertext -2.061 (22 sd), above the annealer on the real text (-1.978). Verdict pass. The key was built on this letter, so this shows the reading is not what fitting alone gives; it does not test single values.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.76; polyphony 0.0; 2 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.978

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: One sentence of the 22 February letter stands nearly word for word in the clear letter to Meyercron of 20 February in the same copybook (found by the repository); the key was fixed on those 32 groups and carried through the rest of the letter from context. No key sheet and no decipherment.
outcome.fraction_read_source: texts/1675-02-22_lindenow_reading.md: 54 of 84 words of the cipher runs plain, one unread, 29 marked [?word] (texts/1675-02-22_lindenow_marks.md). The same count as the project's on issue #679. The three other letters are decoded, not read, and are not in the figure.

texts.label: Biermann to Lindenow, 11 January 1675
texts.note: Decoded with the key of 22 February as it stands: 33 of 57 groups have a value. Runs 'de la mesme [743] que les' and 'avec la Suede'; no sentence.
texts.summary: (Diplomatic) Clear text: Holland deliberates on the entry of Swedish troops into Brandenburg; the cipher holds what some propose the States of Holland should do, not read.

texts.label: Biermann to Lindenow, 18 January 1675
texts.note: Decoded with the key of 22 February as it stands: 12 of 14 groups have a value ('la li s qui y e s [963] i t [693] i n te'). One clause, too short to count.
texts.summary: (Diplomatic) Clear text: the King is satisfied with what Lindenow told the Dutch minister and with something else named in a cipher clause of 14 groups, not read.

texts.label: Biermann to Lindenow, 22 February 1675
texts.note: read_share is by words on the reading file: 84 words in the four cipher runs, one unread ([607]), 29 marked [?word], 54 plain; the same count as the project's on issue #679 (72 of 84 by the first submission's own marks). The 29: 23 words with a value seen once and read from context, four supported only by the fitted April reading, 'les' in the provisional clause, 'mettent' for a disputed sign. The key was built on this letter, so the share is not a test of the key.
texts.summary: (Diplomatic, military) Lindenow's thoughts on Sweden's armament in Germany, the ease of increasing it and what the King might have to fear from it are found prudent, but those who already feel its effects do so little about it that one can only pity them. The treaty draft presented by Count Niels Brahe is wholly to Sweden's advantage with nothing of substance for the King. In clear: the terms of the draft, the Gottorp clauses, the departure of the Duke's envoy, troops gathering towards Norway.

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #721 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Grade given by the reviewer, not by the author of the reading, and entered at the reviewer's request. The four cipher runs were read as French against the English translation: coherent, sentence for sentence. 29 of 84 words are marked [?] (single values read from context, the provisional clause, two disputed signs) and [607]+r+G18 is unread, so the text is coherent but raw. Lines R01-R07 of image 71 were checked on the scan against the transcription (66 groups, all agree; R03/3 + or 4 and R06/5 718 or 715 doubtful, as marked); L01-L11 and R08-R10 were checked on 16 Nov in the review of issue #679 (130 groups, all agree). A model's check: no person has read the scan.

texts.label: Biermann to Lindenow, 12 April 1675
texts.note: Decoded with the key of 22 February as it stands: 85 of 123 groups have a value. Runs 'cette', 'il ne les', 'mesler en se m u le', 'la mo u r', 'sa [781] i s sa n ce'. The contributor's fitted reading (a marriage proposal for a princess) is in NOTES.md and is not counted.
texts.summary: (Diplomatic) Clear text: the Swedish ambassador and the article on the Treaty of Gottorp; the cipher appears to concern a marriage proposal that should be kept apart from the other business, not read.

outcome.notes: Filed as read in part: one letter, 54 of 84 words with single values read from context counted as holes. The treaty sentence rests on the clear parallel; the military paragraph is read from context with one verb unread and one clause provisional. The transcriptions were checked on the scan by a model, not blind, and by no person.
